youtube.title: Rust Day 4: Why Can't I Change x? (let vs mut) 🦀 #Shorts

scenes.say: Rust, day four. Why won't Rust let you change x?

scenes.heading: Try this
scenes.caption: E0384: cannot assign twice
scenes.say: Write let x equals five, then x equals six. It doesn't compile: cannot assign twice to immutable variable.
scenes.captions: Write let x = 5, then x = 6. It doesn't compile: cannot assign twice to immutable variable.

scenes.heading: Immutable by default
scenes.say: In Rust, variables are immutable by default. Once x is set, it can't change, so code that relies on it stays correct.

scenes.heading: Add mut
scenes.caption: prints 5, then 6
scenes.say: Need to change it? Add mut. Now x goes from five to six.
scenes.captions: Need to change it? Add mut. Now x goes from 5 to 6.

scenes.heading: mut means: this will change
scenes.say: mut also tells anyone reading your code that this value will change.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: let is immutable, let mut can change, and E0384 means you assigned twice.
